knowledge.the_winter_rescue.generator_t1: Copper carries heat. It might help adapt the ship's core to a furnace that can warm the soil.
To use the salvaged core in a generator, reconnect its heat paths and fill the gaps in its casing.
Turn the deflectors inside the core to guide each heat path to its matching outlet, then stamp the drawing.
Heat can now reach all the outlets.
Rotate and place the fragments to fill every empty cell in the core, then stamp the drawing.
The core is ready to fit into a tier-one generator core assembly. Claim the energy core after completing the research.
Craft a tier-one generator core from an energy core, bricks, and copper ingots.
Use an Engineer's Hammer to form an assembled tier-one generator.
knowledge.the_winter_rescue.thermos.idea: A wooden cup holds just one drink. Try fitting a wooden shell around a copper liner to carry several drinks in one container.
knowledge.the_winter_rescue.thermos.link: Observe a wooden cup and link the observation at the drawing desk. Drinking cold water can also inspire the idea.
knowledge.the_winter_rescue.thermos.proj: Arrange the thermos parts at the drawing desk, then make your first thermos at the experiment table. Finish the research so your team can craft more.
knowledge.the_winter_rescue.thermos.draw: Fit every part in the tray into the thermos outline. Empty spaces are fine. Stamp the drawing and advance to assemble the wooden shell and copper liner.
knowledge.the_winter_rescue.thermos.expe: Assemble a Wooden Shell and Copper Liner

Select this experiment at the experiment table, add one copper sheet and one plank, and start. After 10 seconds, take the empty thermos from the output slots and finish the research at the drawing desk.
knowledge.the_winter_rescue.thermos.resu: Unlocks the recipes for crafting a thermos and removing its dye.
